aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abarim.title: Abarim
abarim.note: A range of mountains east of the Dead Sea, looking across at Jericho. Mount Nebo is the peak in it that people know, because that is where Moses stood to see the land he was not going to enter. Israel camped here at the end of the wilderness years.

abelshittim.title: Abelshittim
abelshittim.note: Israel's last camp before crossing the Jordan, on the plains of Moab opposite Jericho. The name means meadow of acacias, and most of the Old Testament just calls it Shittim. Balaam was hired from here, and this is where Israel went after Baal-peor.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

ahihud-2.title: Ahihud
ahihud-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ahihud-2.note: When the land west of the Jordan was divided, each tribe sent one leader to work with Eleazar the priest and Joshua. Ahihud was Asher's.

ain-2.title: Ain
ain-2.note: Named once, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

almondilathaim.title: Almondilathaim
almondilathaim.note: Better known as Almon-diblathaim. Israel camped here in Moabite territory, between Dibon-gad and the mountains of Abarim, one of the last stops before the plains of Moab opposite Jericho.

alush.title: Alush
alush.note: Israel camped here between Dophkah and Rephidim, close to the end of the march to Mount Sinai.

ammihud-4.title: Ammihud
ammihud-4.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ammihud-4.note: Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

ammihud-5.title: Ammihud
ammihud-5.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ammihud-5.note: One of 5 men called Ammihud. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in Numbers.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

arad.title: Arad
arad.note: Its king attacked Israel as they came up toward Canaan from the south and took prisoners, and Israel destroyed the town under the ban. The Canaanite city lay about 20 miles south of Hebron, at Tel Arad.

aroer-2.title: Aroer
aroer-2.note: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

ataroth-2.title: Ataroth
ataroth-2.note: Reuben and Gad asked for Ataroth because the pasture was good for their livestock. Several towns east of the Jordan shared the name.

atroth.title: Atroth
atroth.note: Short for Atroth-shophan, a town in Gilead that Gad rebuilt and fortified. Its site is unknown.

azmon.title: Azmon
azmon.note: On Israel's southern border, near the Wadi el-Arish, the Brook of Egypt that marked the southwest edge of the land. Nobody has found the site.

azzan.title: Azzan
azzan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
azzan.note: Paltiel's father, named only so we know whose son the Issachar leader was when the land of Canaan was divided.

baal-meon.title: Baal-meon
baal-meon.note: It was rebuilt by Reuben, a town east of the Jordan known by several names, Beth-baal-meon and Beth-meon among them. The land around it changed hands more than once.

baal-zephon.title: Baal-zephon
baal-zephon.note: A landmark on the shore by the Israelites' last camp before they crossed the sea. Exodus names it in the crossing story and Numbers in the list of wilderness stops.

balaam.title: Balaam
balaam.about: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balaam.note: A prophet, but not an Israelite. Balak of Moab hired him to curse the Israelites. On the way his donkey saw an angel blocking the road that Balaam himself missed, and God made the animal speak to rebuke him.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

bene-jaakan.title: Bene-jaakan
bene-jaakan.note: Sons of Jaakan, a stop on Israel's wilderness route, also called Beeroth Bene-jaakan, wells of the sons of Jaakan. The name likely comes from a clan descended from Jaakan.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beon.title: Beon
beon.note: Beon is a short form of Baal-meon, one of the towns in the Transjordan pastureland Reuben and Gad asked Moses for, to keep their livestock.

beor.title: Beor
beor.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
beor.note: Balaam's father, named whenever Balaam is called son of Beor.

beth-haran.title: Beth-haran
beth-haran.note: It was rebuilt and fortified by the tribe of Gad, east of the Jordan in the plains of Moab. It is generally identified with Beth-haram of Joshua 13:27.

beth-jeshimoth.title: Beth-jeshimoth
beth-jeshimoth.note: Israel's camp on the plains of Moab, the last before they crossed the Jordan into the promised land.

beth-nimrah.title: Beth-Nimrah
beth-nimrah.note: Gad rebuilt this fortified town east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho, after asking for the well-watered land of Gilead for their livestock.

bukki-2.title: Bukki
bukki-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
bukki-2.note: Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

chinnereth.title: Chinnereth
chinnereth.note: Before anyone called it Gennesaret or Tiberias, the lake was the Sea of Chinnereth, named for a fortified Canaanite city on its northwest shore. The town fell inside Naphtali's land. Under the plural Chinneroth it named the whole district, which Ben-hadad of Syria raided in Baasha's reign.

chislon.title: Chislon
chislon.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
chislon.note: The father of Elidad, the leader from the tribe of Benjamin picked to help divide Canaan, and nothing else is known of him.

dibon.title: Dibon
dibon.note: A Moabite city Israel took and rebuilt. King Mesha names it on the Moabite Stone as one of his own building projects.

dophkah.title: Dophkah
dophkah.note: A wilderness camp in Sinai between the desert of Sin and Alush. The name is related to a word for smelting, and some connect it with the Egyptian turquoise and copper mines at Serabit el-Khadim.

ebronah.title: Ebronah
ebronah.note: Israel camped here near Ezion-geber on the way through the wilderness, and moved on.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elealeh.title: Elealeh
elealeh.note: Reuben rebuilt this town on the grazing plateau east of the Jordan for its herds. By Isaiah's and Jeremiah's time Moab had it back, and both name it in their oracles. The ruin el-Al, just northeast of Heshbon, is the site.

eleazar.title: Eleazar
eleazar.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eleazar.note: Aaron's third son. Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, and Eleazar became high priest after his father. He worked with Moses on the second census and with Joshua on dividing the land, and his line held the high priesthood for most of the history after.

elidad.title: Elidad
elidad.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elidad.note: Son of Chislon, Benjamin's chief among the twelve leaders who helped divide Canaan.

elim.title: Elim
elim.note: After the bitter water at Marah, Israel came to Elim, with twelve springs and seventy palm trees. It is commonly placed at Wadi Gharandal, an oasis on Sinai's western coast road that still grows palms.

elizaphan-2.title: Elizaphan
elizaphan-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elizaphan-2.note: Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

ephod.title: Ephod
ephod.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ephod.note: Father of Hanniel, Manasseh's leader in dividing Canaan. Nothing else is recorded of him, and he has nothing to do with the priest's garment.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

eshcol.title: Eshcol
eshcol.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eshcol.note: An Amorite ally who helped Abraham get Lot back from Chedorlaomer. The Valley of Eshcol near Hebron, probably named for him or his clan, is where the twelve spies cut the huge cluster of grapes.

etham.title: Etham
etham.note: Israel's third camp out of Egypt, on the edge of the wilderness. From there God turned Moses back toward Pi-hahiroth to draw Pharaoh after them. It was near the north end of the Gulf of Suez, but nobody knows exactly where.

evi.title: Evi
evi.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
evi.note: One of five Midianite kings killed in the war against Midian that followed Baal-peor. His land is recalled in Joshua among what was later allotted. Nothing more is known of him.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hanniel-2.title: Hanniel
hanniel-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hanniel-2.note: Moses picked him to speak for Manasseh when the land was divided.

haradah.title: Haradah
haradah.note: The name means fright, and it was the twenty-fifth stop on the wilderness route. Numbers 33:24-25 is all there is.

hashmonah.title: Hashmonah
hashmonah.note: One of the stops on the wilderness route, a little before Moseroth and near Mount Hor. The name may have to do with fatness or fruitfulness, and nobody knows where it was.

hazar-addar.title: Hazar-addar
hazar-addar.note: The border point near Kadesh-barnea on the south of the promised land, which Joshua 15:3 calls Addar.

hazar-enan.title: Hazar-enan
hazar-enan.note: The corner of the promised land in the northeast, in Numbers 34:9-10, and again on the northern line of Ezekiel's restored Israel. It means village of springs. It probably sat in the Anti-Lebanon near Damascus, but nobody has found it.

hazeroth.title: Hazeroth
hazeroth.note: The third camp after Sinai, in the wilderness of Paran. Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses here over his Cushite wife. Miriam was struck with a skin disease and healed when Moses prayed for her.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hoglah.title: Hoglah
hoglah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hoglah.note: One of Zelophehad's five daughters. They asked Moses for their father's land, got it, and set a precedent for Israel.

hor.title: Hor
hor.note: Aaron died on Mount Hor, at the edge of Edom near the end of the wandering. His priestly garments were taken off him in sight of the people, and they buried him on the mountain.

hor-2.title: Hor
hor-2.note: Named twice, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

hor-hagidgad.title: Hor-hagidgad
hor-hagidgad.note: A wilderness camp in the list of stations in Numbers, usually taken to be the Gudgodah of Deuteronomy. Its site south of Kadesh has not been fixed.

hur-2.title: Hur
hur-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hur-2.note: Numbers and Joshua name him twice, and he is a king from the wilderness years.

iim.title: Iim
iim.note: The name means ruins, and two places carry it. One is a town in the far south of Judah near Edom; the other is a late stop in the wilderness, just before Israel reached Moab's border.

ije-abarim.title: Ije-abarim
ije-abarim.note: They camped here on the border of Moab late in the journey from Egypt. The name means "ruins of Abarim", after the range east of the Jordan, and the camp itself has not been found.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jaazer.title: Jaazer
jaazer.note: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jair.title: Jair
jair.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jair.note: He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jephunneh.title: Jephunneh
jephunneh.about: Caleb's father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jephunneh.note: Caleb's father, remembered almost entirely as a name in "Caleb son of Jephunneh", which is how the Old Testament tells that Caleb apart from the others.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jogbehah.title: Jogbehah
jogbehah.note: It was one of the towns Gad built and walled east of the Jordan. Gideon went past it on the caravan route, chasing the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna.

jogli.title: Jogli
jogli.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jogli.note: Bukki's father. Bukki led the tribe of Dan when the land of Canaan was divided. Jogli is known only through him.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

jotbath.title: Jotbath
jotbath.note: They camped here in the wilderness, between Hor-hagidgad and Ebronah. Moses remembered it as a land of brooks of water, which in that desert stood out. Nobody knows for sure where it was.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kadesh.title: Kadesh
kadesh.note: Kadesh-barnea, Israel's main camp in the wilderness of Zin. Moses sent the twelve spies from there, Miriam died there, and there he struck the rock and lost his way into Canaan. It is usually identified with Ain el-Qudeis or Ain el-Qudeirat, where a fortress of the Israelite period has been dug up.

kadeshbarnea.title: Kadeshbarnea
kadeshbarnea.note: An oasis in the wilderness of Zin, on Canaan's southern edge, where Israel camped for much of the wandering years. The spies went out from here, and the people's fear at their report got that whole generation sentenced to die in the desert. Later it marked the southern boundary of the land.

kehelathah.title: Kehelathah
kehelathah.note: A stop on the wilderness march, between Rissah and Mount Shepher. The name is related to the Hebrew word for assembly, and the site cannot be found today.

kemuel-3.title: Kemuel
kemuel-3.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kemuel-3.note: A tribal leader of Ephraim, appointed to help divide the land under Joshua.

kenath.title: Kenath
kenath.note: In Bashan, east of the Jordan, taken when Israel moved in and renamed Nobah after the man who took it. It is generally identified with Qanawat on the slopes of Jebel Hauran, where Roman ruins still stand, a theatre among them.

kenezite.title: Kenezite
kenezite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kenezite.note: Caleb, one of the two spies who stayed faithful, is called a Kenizzite. The clan came from Kenaz and was tied to Edom in Genesis, then folded into Judah.

kibroth-hattaavah.title: Kibroth-hattaavah
kibroth-hattaavah.note: "The graves of craving." The people were sick of manna and demanded meat, and God sent quails in a huge flock. A plague broke out while they ate, and the dead were buried where they fell, so the camp was named for what they had wanted. Moses brought it up again years later when he listed the times they had provoked God.

kiriathaim.title: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim.note: It started out as a town of Reuben's and ended up in Moab, on Jeremiah's list of the cities God's judgment would fall on.

libnah-2.title: Libnah
libnah-2.note: Named twice, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

machir.title: Machir
machir.about: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
machir.note: Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

mahlah.title: Mahlah
mahlah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
mahlah.note: Zelophehad had five daughters and no son, and Mahlah was one of them; their plea to Moses to inherit his land changed the law.

makheloth.title: Makheloth
makheloth.note: Somewhere between Haradah and Tahath on Israel's march, in the list of camps in Numbers 33.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

marah.title: Marah
marah.note: Three days past the sea, the first water Israel found was too bitter to drink. Moses threw a piece of wood in at the Lord's word and it turned sweet, and God gave them a statute there and tested them. Many put it at Ain Hawarah in Sinai, a spring that is still brackish.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

migdol.title: Migdol
migdol.note: "Tower," a fortified point on Egypt's northeastern border. One Migdol is on Israel's route to the crossing of the sea. Jeremiah names a Migdol where Jewish refugees settled in Egypt, and Ezekiel's "from Migdol to Syene" means the whole length of the country.

milcah-2.title: Milcah
milcah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
milcah-2.note: A different woman from Nahor's wife. This Milcah is one of the five sisters in Numbers 27 who asked for their father's land.

mithcah.title: Mithcah
mithcah.note: "Sweetness." One of the stops late in the forty years of wandering, in Numbers 33, with no word on why it got the name and no known site.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebo.title: Nebo
nebo.note: The mountain in Moab where Moses looked over the promised land before he died, taken as Jebel Neba on the ridge of Pisgah east of the Dead Sea. A Reubenite town nearby had the same name, and the oracles against Moab condemn it.

nimrah.title: Nimrah
nimrah.note: Reuben and Gad wanted this ground east of the Jordan for their herds because it was good cattle land, and it is usually identified with Beth-nimrah.

noah-2.title: Noah
noah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
noah-2.note: Not the man of the flood. This Noah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who went to Moses and won the right to inherit their father's land, since there was no son.

nobah.title: Nobah
nobah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
nobah.note: He took the Amorite town of Kenath east of the Jordan and renamed it after himself, and the town turns up again as a landmark on Gideon's route.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

oboth.title: Oboth
oboth.note: Israel camped at Oboth after the bronze serpent. Where exactly it sat along the route is not known.

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

paltiel.title: Paltiel
paltiel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
paltiel.note: Two men. One was the leader from Issachar picked to help divide the land among the tribes. The other, son of Laish, was given Michal by King Saul after David fled, and he lost her again when David took her back.

parnach.title: Parnach
parnach.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
parnach.note: Elizaphan led Zebulun when the land of Canaan was being divided, and Parnach was his father, named only to identify the son.

pedahel.title: Pedahel
pedahel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
pedahel.note: Son of Ammihud, and the leader from Naphtali whom Moses picked to help share out Canaan among the tribes. His name means "God has redeemed."

peor.title: Peor
peor.note: Balak took Balaam up this peak in Moab for one last try at cursing Israel. It came out a blessing again, the one about a star and a scepter rising out of Israel.

phinehas.title: Phinehas
phinehas.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phinehas.note: Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.

pi-hahiroth.title: Pi-hahiroth
pi-hahiroth.note: Israel doubled back from Etham and camped here beside the sea, and Pharaoh's army came up behind them. It was here that Moses stretched out his hand over the water.

punon.title: Punon
punon.note: Israel camped here between Zalmonah and Oboth, and it is identified with Phaeno, where early Christian writers placed Roman copper mines.

raamses.title: Raamses
raamses.note: The Israelites built Raamses, also spelled Rameses, as a store city for Pharaoh in the eastern Nile Delta, alongside Pithom. When they left Egypt, this is where they set out from.

reba.title: Reba
reba.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
reba.note: One of five Midianite kings killed in the war Moses ordered shortly before his death. His land was later counted in Reuben's share. Joshua 13:21 lists him again with the others.

rekem.title: Rekem
rekem.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
rekem.note: One of the five Midianite kings Israel killed in the days of Moses. The same name belongs to a man in Manasseh's genealogy.

rephidim.title: Rephidim
rephidim.note: Israel camped here near Sinai and ran out of water. The people nearly stoned Moses, and he struck the rock at Horeb and water came out. Amalek attacked them at the same place.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

riblah-2.title: Riblah
riblah-2.note: Named once, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

rimmon-parez.title: Rimmon-parez
rimmon-parez.note: A camp in the wilderness between Rithmah and Libnah, named only in Numbers 33, and its site is unknown.

rissah.title: Rissah
rissah.note: Israel stopped here between Libnah and Kehelathah. The name may mean ruin, or dew.

rithmah.title: Rithmah
rithmah.note: One of the camps in the itinerary of Numbers 33. It is named for the broom shrub common in the desert.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

shapper.title: Shapper
shapper.note: Mount Shepher, a stop in the wilderness between Kehelathah and Haradah. The name means beauty or brightness. The text gives nothing more.

shebam.title: Shebam
shebam.note: Good grazing land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon, which Reuben and Gad asked for because of their flocks.

shelomi.title: Shelomi
shelomi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shelomi.note: His son Ahihud was picked to help divide Canaan among the tribes. He was an Asherite, and Numbers 34:27 names him for that.

shepham.title: Shepham
shepham.note: A point on the eastern border Israel was meant to have, between Hazar-enan and Riblah (Numbers 34:10–11). Nobody can place it exactly.

shiphtan.title: Shiphtan
shiphtan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shiphtan.note: Father of Kemuel, Ephraim's man on the commission that divided Canaan among the tribes (Numbers 34:24).

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sin.title: Sin
sin.note: Israel crossed the Wilderness of Sin after leaving Egypt, and when the people complained of hunger this is where the manna and the quail first came.

sinai.title: Sinai
sinai.note: Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

succoth-2.title: Succoth
succoth-2.note: Israel's first campsite after leaving Egypt.

tahath-2.title: Tahath
tahath-2.note: A wilderness camp between Makheloth and Terah in the list of Numbers 33, and nobody knows where it was.

tarah-2.title: Tarah
tarah-2.note: Named twice, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

tirzah-2.title: Tirzah
tirzah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
tirzah-2.note: She was the youngest of Zelophehad's five daughters, named with her sisters each time the family's inheritance comes up.

zalmonah.title: Zalmonah
zalmonah.note: Israel camped here after Mount Hor. The name probably has to do with shade, and it is usually put somewhere in the Arabah south of the Dead Sea, though nobody has pinned it down.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zedad.title: Zedad
zedad.note: They put it on the northern border of the land, near Hamath, both in Moses' description and again in Ezekiel's vision. Some identify it with the Syrian village of Sadad.

zelophehad.title: Zelophehad
zelophehad.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zelophehad.note: He died in the wilderness with five daughters and no sons. They went to Moses and asked for their father's land, and they got it, and the law of inheritance changed because of them.

zin.title: Zin
zin.note: The Wilderness of Zin, where Kadesh lay. Miriam died there, and there Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it.

ziphron.title: Ziphron
ziphron.note: A point on the northern border of the land Moses described, southeast of Hamath. Nobody has found it.

zur-2.title: Zur
zur-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zur-2.note: A Midianite chief killed in Israel's war against Midian. Phinehas had already killed his daughter Cozbi over the idolatry that brought the plague.
